title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 162
paragraphs: Now these Phocaians were the first of the Hellenes to make long voyages, and it was they who discovered the Adriatic, Tyrsenia, Iberia, and Tartessos. They made these voyages not in round ships, but in vessels of fifty oars. When they came to Tartessos, they became friends with the king of the Tartessians, whose name was Arganthonios: he ruled over the Tartessians for eighty years and lived altogether one hundred and twenty. With this man the Phocaians became so exceedingly friendly that at first he bade them leave Ionia and dwell wherever they desired in his own land. When he did not persuade the Phocaians to do this, afterwards, hearing from them of the Mede and how his power was increasing, he gave them money to build a wall around their city. He did this without stinting, for the circuit of the wall is many furlongs in extent, and it is built entirely of large stones closely fitted together.
